clauses: Count distinct films that have at least one inventory copy, per rating.
Count inventory copies (inventory rows) per rating, so a film with several copies counts several times.
Count only copies currently on the shelf (not out on an unreturned rental) as in stock.
readings: Looking at the films we have in stock by `rating`, which ratings have more films in inventory than the average rating does? Give me a single row with the total films in stock across those above-average ratings and, on average, how far above the across-rating average they are (no rounding). Count only copies currently on the shelf (not out on an unreturned rental) as in stock.
queries:
WITH c AS (
  SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) AS n
  FROM film f
  JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
a AS (
  SELECT AVG(n) AS avg_n FROM c
)
SELECT SUM(c.n) AS total_films_in_stock, AVG(c.n - a.avg_n) AS avg_above_average
FROM c, a
WHERE c.n > a.avg_n;
WITH c AS (
  SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM inventory i
  JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
a AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM c
)
SELECT SUM(c.cnt) AS total_films_in_stock,
       AVG(c.cnt - a.avg_cnt) AS avg_above_average
FROM c, a
WHERE c.cnt > a.avg_cnt;
WITH stock AS (
  SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS n
  FROM inventory i
  JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM rental r
    WHERE r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id AND r.return_date IS NULL
  )
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
avg_stock AS (
  SELECT AVG(n) AS a FROM stock
)
SELECT SUM(n) AS total_films_in_stock, AVG(n - a) AS avg_above_average
FROM stock, avg_stock
WHERE n > a;
